1: Some careers deliver projects. Others leave behind a standard, a method… and the people who carry it forward.
2: Honorary Fellow, P-C-I… conferred by the Board of an independent professional body — in recognition of distinguished contribution, leadership and service. Your name — on P-C-I's own public registry… checkable at source.
3: The Project Controls Institute is an independent professional body — a Delaware Non-Stock Corporation — built to give the discipline a shared standard, an independent credential… and a professional home for the A-I era. Its published Body of Knowledge sets thirteen domains and sixty-one knowledge areas. And every credential it confers… is entered on a registry anyone can check.
4: It involves no examination. The record is the evidence… and the Board weighs it. It is separate from P-C-I's examined certifications — P-C-L A-I, P-F-L A-I and P-M-L A-I. Every application is considered individually… and recognition is conferred solely at the Board's discretion.
5: If you have led teams, shaped standards, taught, published or governed — in project controls, cost control, finance, project management, or a closely related discipline — you may apply.
6: From construction and energy… to technology, aviation, project finance, government and academia. Wherever leadership shapes OUTCOMES, your contribution counts.
7: The floor is eight years of professional experience… three of them at managerial level — leading teams, functions, programmes or budgets. The bar is higher — a demonstrable record of distinguished contribution. Meeting the criteria does not guarantee recognition.
8: P-C-I charges no nomination, assessment, or credential fee. Optional extras — such as attending an awards ceremony — are charged separately, and play no part in the decision. Recognition is awarded solely on merit. One application… your profile, résumé, career history and evidence — reviewed confidentially by the Board.
9: You need no sponsor to be considered. You put your own record forward. The Board then assesses it against published criteria… on the evidence — and does so confidentially.
10: Those recognised are entered on P-C-I's own public registry… checkable at source by anyone — labelled honorary, never a passed examination.
11: If recognised, you may also be given access to the P-C-I student portal, and the Institute's learning resources — video lectures, course material, and the simulation lab. The same terms may extend to study through Certuvo, P-C-I's official preparation platform… and invitations to selected P-C-I A-I events — all subject to current programme terms.
12: Tell the Board which discipline your contribution aligns to — project controls, project finance, or project management. Optional… and it confers no examined certification.
13: If your work has outlasted the projects it was done on… it deserves to be recognised. Apply for the Board's consideration — at P-C-I-A-I dot org. Questions… to Members, at P-C-I-A-I dot org.
